daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

National Police Chief Suyudi Arto Seno executed a major reorganization of police leadership, installing 27 new officials including 19 regional police chiefs shortly after his inauguration. The reshuffle included the appointment of Irjen Dadang Hartanto as Kapolda Metro, though he had not yet been formally sworn in as he remained on umrah pilgrimage. The reorganization has drawn scrutiny, with analysts describing it as "Kapolri Baru, Mutasi Besar, dan Bayang-bayang 2029" and raising questions about the political implications ahead of the 2029 elections.

  • A DPR lawmaker endorsed President Prabowo's cabinet reshuffle and leadership changes across government institutions.
  • President Prabowo's appointment of Anwar Usman to Wantimpres has generated controversy given the former Constitutional Court chief's family ties to the president.
  • The Presidential Advisory Council (Wantimpres) appointment has been characterized as a potential "trap of accommodative politics" by political observers.
  • Commission III of the DPR visited the residence of Kapolri Suyudi, with member Habiburokhman describing it as a longstanding tradition.
  • The Supreme Court granted the impeachment of Gowa Regent Husniah Talenrang, though the decision does not automatically end her tenure, and the Ministry of Home Affairs is awaiting a formal proposal from Gowa's regional legislature.
  • The Head of the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) discovered foundations demanding payments per meal from kitchen partners in the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program and pledged to cut off any foundation collecting such levies.
  • Analysts are questioning why President Prabowo continues searching for the right communications chief.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Russia emphasized that its naval visit to Indonesia carries a "friendship mission" as Russian warships arrived at Indonesian ports. Separately, the leader of the Republic of Tatarstan is scheduled to visit Indonesia in early November, according to the Russian ambassador. Indonesia's TNI Commander inspected preparations for the 81st anniversary ceremony of the Indonesian National Armed Forces at Cilangkap.

  • Indonesia is pushing to fast-track a comprehensive economic partnership with the European Union before the EU's Generalized System of Preferences expires.
  • Indonesia and G20 countries have rejected the use of food as a weapon of geopolitical pressure in a joint statement.
  • Indonesia seeks to strengthen industrial cooperation and human resource development with Germany, while the German ambassador described industrial cooperation as a significant achievement in bilateral relations.
  • Indonesia is preparing a Sheikh Yusuf Al Makassari exhibition to be held in Amsterdam.
  • China donated 100 book titles to Indonesia's National Library.

Other

The government established a complaint channel to protect consumers whose mobile data plans expire prematurely, with Kompas reporting on operator compliance in preventing quota forfeiture. The initiative follows widespread consumer complaints about telecommunications providers allowing unused internet quota to expire. Bank Indonesia's research on how Digital Rupiah shapes Indonesia's economy highlighted the potential transformation of the country's payment systems.

  • The price of Antam gold fell significantly over the course of a week.
  • An academic called for accelerating the integration of downstream industries and energy transition efforts.
  • The Minister of Religion said that through the Garuda program, madrasah can now compete with other schools, while approximately 25 percent of Indonesian schools now offer coding and artificial intelligence subjects.
  • The Health Ministry is expanding healthcare services in Papua Highlands, while the Ministry of Marine Affairs promoted low-carbon aquaculture to boost exports.
  • The Ministry of Transportation emphasized that transportation safety is the primary focus heading into the rainy season, while the government is bolstering oversight of overloaded vehicles.
